lines.trans: Kostya, hi, are you very busy right now?
Hi, Nastya, no, I am completely free.
Then come with me into the quiet room.
Wait a second, where exactly are we going?
I wanted to ask you seriously for a long time.
I will listen to you with pleasure now.
Do you want us to start dating?
Nastya, I just got a little confused.
Or do you not want this at all?
Of course I want to, I like you very much!

meanings.note: возвращаться домой = to come back home; к + dative = to someone

examples.text: Запомните: зло всегда возвращается к правителю.
examples.trans: Remember: evil always comes back to the ruler.

встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, go out

meanings.en: to date, go out with each other
meanings.note: Мы встречаемся = we're dating. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet; to date, go out', paired with 'встретиться'.

meanings.en: to meet up, see each other
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet; to date, go out', paired with 'встретиться'.

examples.trans: We've been going out for a month already.

examples.text: Мы уже месяц встречаемся. Мне надоело уже.
examples.trans: We've been going out for a month already. I'm tired of it already.

meanings.en: to hear out, listen attentively to
meanings.note: Listen until the end. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'слушать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to listen to, hear out', paired with 'выслушивать'.

examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully.
The judge patiently heard out the witness's testimony.

examples.text: Сначала выслушай меня очень внимательно, Аркаша.
examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully, Arkasha.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.note: with present: Я давно здесь = I've been here a long time
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

meanings.note: Of a person: я занят = I'm busy. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy; occupied, taken').
of a place: здесь занято = it's occupied
In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.
вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.
Тошнит от = sick of. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!

растеряться.gloss: to become confused, to be at a loss

meanings.en: to become confused, to be at a loss
meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'теряться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to become confused', forming an aspectual pair with 'теряться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Nastya, I just got a little confused.

examples.text: Я в полном шоке и страшно растерялся.
examples.trans: I am in total shock and terribly lost.

meanings.note: Секунду! = One second! / Just a moment!

meanings.en: to ask (a question, or someone: спросить у кого-то)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спрашивать'.

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
